traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Opiliaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; veins pinnate; stipules absent; plants usually hermaphrodite, often dioecious; ovary superior or half inferior; floral cup absent; stems woody; flowers in panicles, in racemes, in spikes or in umbels; flowers actinomorphic; perianth usually tepals, sometimes sepals and petals; fruit drupe; parts of each whorl 4 to 5; stamens 4 to 5; carpels 2 to 5. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
